basis: Disorders arising in or affecting the uvea; immune mechanisms do not apply across this umbrella.
Congenital joint contractures and mandibular hypoplasia define skeletal involvement; no evidence supports additional organ damage.
Finger contractures and skeletal abnormalities define disease; cardiac septal defects are annotated frequent (30-79%), although reports are limited.
Tendon inflammation, usually from overuse; inflammation alone does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Inherited dilated cardiomyopathy with reduced ventricular function; tachypnea does not establish intrinsic pulmonary damage.
Mitochondrial metabolic myopathy with cataracts; progressive hearing loss occurs in 30-79%; developmental delay/callosal hypoplasia (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Eosinophilia with immune-mediated muscle/fascial disease; persistent skin induration affects roughly half; neurologic and pulmonary involvement omitted by cap.
Benign neoplasm originating in the rectum.
Neurodevelopmental disease, achalasia and alacrima define syndrome; myopathy reported in 2/2 assessed patients; hyperkeratosis (2/2) omitted by cap.
Selective antibody deficiency; recurrent respiratory infections are separate infections, while bronchiectasis is occasional (5-29%).
Squamous carcinoma originating in the skin of the external ear.
TYMP metabolic disease with neuropathy and intestinal dysfunction; ptosis/ophthalmoplegia approximately universal; myopathy and hearing loss (45%) omitted by cap.
Skeletal malformations, microcephaly/intellectual disability and deafness define syndrome; cataract is also a defining diagnostic feature.
Sensorineural deafness with ovarian endocrine failure; intellectual disability and sensorimotor neuropathy reported in 2/2, cerebellar atrophy in 1/2.
Psychotic and mood disorder without defining damage to an organ axis.
Klebsiella infection directly causing pulmonary inflammation and injury.
Follicular ichthyosis and alopecia with ocular disease; blepharitis 8/12, keratitis and cataract each 4/12 support structural ocular involvement.
Peripheral neuroblastic tumour arising from sympathetic neural tissue; no additional organ of origin is specified.
Inherited retinal degeneration with rod-cone dystrophy and visual loss.
Red-cell aplasia with mandibulofacial dysostosis; cleft palate and developmental delay each 2/2; hearing loss 1/2 omitted by cap.
Benign neoplasm originating in the renal cortex.
Trichosporon fungal infection; umbrella includes superficial and disseminated forms without a consistently affected additional organ.
Chronic venous valve damage defines syndrome; persistent dermatitis and ulceration mark more severe disease, without clear evidence of >=30% across all cases.
Congenital malposition of the urethral opening; the urethra belongs to the renal axis.
Syndromic intellectual disability with pyramidal and movement abnormalities; congestive heart failure is annotated frequent (30-79%); macroorchidism alone is not endocrine dysfunction.
